evidence.description: The BrazeService class uses a public static shared instance, making it a singleton.

candidates.explanation: The use of a public static shared instance for BrazeService makes it a singleton. Singletons can make unit testing difficult and can lead to shared state issues across the application.
candidates.title: Singleton Pattern Usage

evidence.description: The Task block initiates asynchronous work (refreshAPNRegistrationIfNeeded and APNConsent.requestIfNeeded) without any mechanism to track, cancel, or handle errors of the individual tasks.

candidates.explanation: Calling Task without storing a reference or providing a way to manage the lifecycle of the asynchronous operations can lead to unexpected behavior if the service is deinitialized or if the operations need to be cancelled.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task Usage

evidence.description: The Task block inside initBraze uses @MainActor to set the inAppMessagePresenter, but it is not awaited, meaning the Braze configuration might be used before the presenter is set.

candidates.explanation: Because the Task in initBraze is not awaited, the Braze instance may be fully configured and active before the inAppMessagePresenter is assigned, potentially causing missed in-app messages during the initialization phase.
candidates.title: Potential Race Condition in Initialization

evidence.description: The notificationAuthorizationStatus property is updated asynchronously via retrieveUserCurrentNotificationAuthStatus.

candidates.explanation: The notificationAuthorizationStatus property is updated asynchronously. This means that other parts of the code reading this property might receive stale or outdated information immediately after a request for consent is made.
candidates.title: Delayed State Consistency

evidence.description: The updateID function checks if the id is different from braze?.user.id before calling changeUser.

candidates.explanation: The updateID function checks if the provided id matches the current braze.user.id. If the braze object is nil, the check will pass, but the subsequent call to braze?.changeUser(userId: id) will do nothing, making the check partially redundant or potentially misleading in intent.
candidates.title: Redundant State Check
